topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's importance and warns about the complexity of complement terminology before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic framework for understanding complement as a protein-cleavage cascade centred on C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition produces enough surface-bound C3b to trigger complement activity.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes the elimination of pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains bacterial mechanisms for evading complement, including how protein A's antibody-binding mechanism can be exploited clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
